subject: GreenArc pilot: request for runway after integration blockers
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@greenarc.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Leah Owens <leah.owens@greenarc.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Sep 2026 11:12:00 -0400
Subject: Pilot onboarding — stalled by adapter mismatch, asking for runway

Hi Marissa,

We're excited about the pilot but hit a blocker in our final integration sprint. Our infra team found an incompatibility between your SDK's webhook handshake and our API gateway when payloads exceed 12KB; it's causing repeated auth failures and queue backpressure. We've attached a short trace (greenarc-integration-log.txt) and a stack excerpt.

Because of this we can't complete the end-to-end QA before our planned demo next week. We're hoping Redwood could grant a short extension to the pilot window (and a small sandbox credit top-up) so we can finish the fix and run a conclusive demo for our execs. If possible: +30 days on the pilot and 100k tokens (or equivalent sandbox hours).

Leah and I are happy to join an engineering call; we can share access to a repro and the logs. Appreciate any flexibility — this is a strategic PoC for us and we'd like to keep momentum.

Thanks,
Samir Patel
Head of Product
GreenArc Industries

Attachment: greenarc-integration-log.txt (text, 28KB)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Sep 2026 17:05:00 +0000
Subject: Fwd: Pilot onboarding — stalled by adapter mismatch, asking for runway

Looping you both in — Samir from GreenArc is asking for a 30-day extension + sandbox top-up after an integration mismatch hit their demo prep. They included a log (attached).

Quick context: GreenArc is in a paid pilot (deal GA-2026-09-PILOT). They've been actively testing our webhook + adapter flow; engineering says this looks like a payload-size edge case with our SDK's default chunking.

David — can you review the log and advise whether we can: 1) provide a short-term config workaround they can patch in their gateway, and 2) propose a limited credit bundle we can approve without escalations?

Kimberly — if engineering signs off on a workaround, would you be comfortable approving a 30-day extension and a token/credits bundle (we should try to avoid setting a precedent for open-ended top-ups).

Goal: respond to GreenArc with a clear yes/no and next steps by end of day tomorrow.

-M

-----Original Message-----
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 23 Sep 2026 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot onboarding — stalled by adapter mismatch, asking for runway

Thanks for the ping and for the log. I pulled the trace — this does look like a chunking edge condition in our client library when the payload header set is large and the gateway truncates headers; the server-side auth token check fails intermittently, which leads to retries and queue buildup on GreenArc's side.

Short-term remediation (low risk): we can recommend they enable simple request chunking (set chunk_size=8KB) in the SDK or use our alternative bearer-header normalization flag. Both are config flips and should be backwards compatible. I can draft a one-page runbook and jump on a 30–45 minute debug call tomorrow to walk their engineers through it.

On credits/extension: from an engineering perspective, a 30-day extension is fair for remediation + re-test. For credits, I'd suggest a conservative goodwill bundle: 75,000 tokens and access to an isolated sandbox instance for staging. That keeps the ask reasonable while giving them runway to demo.

If legal or sales needs to sign off on the number, we can present it as a one-time pilot courtesy (no recurring commitment).

I'll prepare the runbook and be available 2026-09-24 16:00–18:00 UTC — tell me which slot works.

-David

Attachment referenced: none (internal note)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 23 Sep 2026 13:40:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot onboarding — stalled by adapter mismatch, asking for runway

Appreciate the quick analysis. Approve the proposed remediation support + runbook and the 30-day extension. For credits: approve 75,000 tokens and a temporary staging sandbox instance (48-hour spin-up window, idempotent). Please document the credit grant in HubSpot and mark it as a one-time concession tied to GA-2026-09-PILOT.

Marissa — I'll prepare the approval stub (PDF) and a short customer note template you can send to Samir. We should include a single bullet that this is goodwill and doesn't change commercial terms.

Also: please copy Finance via thread if they need the cost sign-off; this is within our quarterly allowance for pilot makegoods.

-Kim

Subject: Re: Pilot onboarding — stalled by adapter mismatch, asking for runway

Hi Samir / Leah —

Thanks for the details and for sending the trace. We reviewed this with engineering and can help you unblock. Here is what we can commit to immediately: 

- 30-day extension to your pilot window (new end date: 2026-10-23).
- 75,000 token goodwill credit applied to your sandbox environment and a temporary isolated staging instance for your verification (we'll provide access instructions).
- Engineering support: David Kim will send a short runbook with a config workaround (recommended chunk_size=8KB or enable header-normalization flag) and is available for a debug call tomorrow at 17:00 UTC.

I've attached the approval stub for your records. This is a one-time courtesy to help you complete the demo and does not change the commercial terms of the pilot. Please confirm the debug call slot and whether you want an hour or 30 minutes. We'll get the sandbox spun up once you confirm.

Next steps:
1) Confirm preferred debug slot (David prefers 17:00 UTC 24 Sep).
2) Leah to share temporary staging credentials or allowlist our IPs for the sandbox.
3) We'll apply the credit and send access details within 24 hours of confirmation.

Happy to help get you across the finish line.

Best,
